addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hera-session: HERA session-init — walks the human through device-card resolution, notebook bootstrap, and JupyterLab preflight on the toploader PC, then writes a session-context file and emits the launch command for the hera tactical agent. (Tools: All tools)

- hera-tactical: HERA tactical — drives measurement sessions with a human operator at the controls. Protocol only; machine facts come from the deployed rig card. Campaign scope set by the session brief. Reads rig card, device card, and live notebook; lands runnable cells via nb-collab. (Tools: All tools)

- iris: IRIS — chat-first collaborator for live toploader measurement sessions. Boots from prior state, follows the operator's lead, types cells when asked. Same tool surface as HERA tactical but inverted social contract — the human drives, IRIS supports. (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# QC0426 / VTI / 3LGr — session brief: bring-up then classify
2	
3	*A live HERA session on a cooled, wired, unknown-stacking device,
4	structured as **two phases with an explicit gate between them**. Phase 1
5	(prep & characterize) takes the device from cooled-and-wired to a
6	blessed measurement configuration — recipe-encoded, mux-automated device
7	bring-up; driving it is half the session's purpose. Phase 2 (classify)
8	runs the stacking investigation on phase 1's groundwork.*
9	
10	## Contract
11	
12	HERA drives via `hera-tactical`; the operator executes every cell —
13	execution is approval, declining is veto (including **interrupting a
14	running sweep cell**, which is always the operator's prerogative;
15	partial runs land readable); Zack supervises remotely. The phase gate
16	(below) adds one session-level handshake of the same kind.
17	
18	## Starting state
19	
20	A trilayer-graphene device (`QC0426`) is **cold (≈ 1.2–1.3 K), wired,
21	and unknown-stacking**. The device card describes what is physically
22	true: gate stack, contact map, instrument rack, the QSwitch routing
23	maps + calibrated `settle_s` (bring-up record complete), and the **gate
24	operating limits**, provided by the operator and committed as validators
25	at session start (not range-found this session).
26	
27	**Provided to you up front (operator sets these — do not re-derive):**
28	**all three gate operating limits** — top gate (`dc205_volt` / `k_tg`),
29	back gate (`k_bg.volt`), and Si (`k_2410`). No gate is range-found this
30	session; commit each as its validator. The geometry ceiling is the hard
31	fence behind the TG numbers.
32	
33	What the card deliberately does NOT carry, and what **phase 1
34	establishes**: the **CNP-line constants + capacitance calibration** and
35	a **workable contact configuration**.
36	
37	## Blocklist
38	
39	- `device-init/silicon-backgate-survey.md` — not run this session.
40	- `device-init/gate-range-finding.md` — not run this session.
41	- `device-init/gate-range-finding-vti.md` — not run this session.
42	- `device-init/gate-leakage-survey.md` — not run this session.
43	
44	## Data isolation — strict this session
45	
46	**No prior measurement data exists for you.** Do not read other
47	campaign or session directories — not the 2026-06 campaign dirs, not
48	any other session directory. Your only inputs: this brief, the device
49	card, the rig card, the recipes/corpus docs they name, and the data
50	this session produces in `./data/`. If a comparison seems to need prior
51	data, the recipes' first-session branches apply (there are no
52	designated references; `reentry-baseline` is N/A by its own When). Ask
53	the operator by name if you believe something is missing. In phase 2,
54	phase 1's data and write-backs are your priors — and your only ones.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Phase 1 — prep & characterize
59	
60	**Goal**: a blessed measurement configuration, evidenced and written
61	back to the device card. Recipes, in dependency order:
62	
63	1. `measurements/contact-survey-2t.md` — automated flavor (QSwitch
64	   bring-up record complete; routing maps and `settle_s` in the card).
65	   **Pick a *workable* configuration, not the optimum**: a source/drain
66	   and three voltage-probe pairs (sr1/sr2/sr3) that are **acceptable,
67	   not best**. Satisfice and move on — contact optimization is not this
68	   session's purpose.
69	2. `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md` — first gate map on the
70	   chosen configuration → CNP fit → capacitance ratio → D-line designer.
71	
72	**Phase-1 exit contract.** Phase 1 ends when all of:
73	
74	- [ ] **All three gate validators** (TG, BG, Si) committed to the
75	      **provided** operating limits.
76	- [ ] CNP/D-line calibration + capacitance ratio established and
77	      written back to the device card.
78	- [ ] **Workable contact configuration** chosen: a source/drain + three
79	      acceptable probe pairs, with brief evidence each is adequate.
80	- [ ] **Exit report landed in the ana notebook**: one section — what
81	      was established, run-id citations for each item, the blessed
82	      configuration, anomalies still open. Write it for the operator —
83	      it's the gate on phase 2.
84	- [ ] **Operator go.** Phase 2 does not start without it. The exit
85	      report is the ask; the operator's go is the approval. If the go
86	      comes with corrections, fold them in before proceeding.
87	
88	Phase-1 work is tens-of-minutes-scale per step (the contact survey is
89	minutes-per-pair with the mux). No magnet hours belong in phase 1
90	beyond what its recipes themselves require.
91	
92	## Phase 2 — classify (stacking investigation)
93	
94	**Goal**: an evidence-cited, region-resolved stacking call (ABA vs ABC
95	vs mixed vs cannot-tell), per
96	`recipes/investigations/trilayer-stacking-id.md`'s output contract, on
97	the configuration phase 1 blessed.
98	
99	4. `investigations/trilayer-stacking-id.md` — the governing procedure;
100	   its ladder (CNP-vs-D first), Verify suite, and five-part output
101	   contract.
102	5. `measurements/landau-fan.md` — grid design per its Nyquist check and
103	   full cost model (calibrate row overhead from this session's own
104	   sweeps; the magnet is ramp-limited and blocking — fine B is nearly
105	   free).
106	6. `measurements/gatemap.md`, `gatemap-in-field.md`, and the rest
107	   of the corpus: available under your scope rules — off-arc
108	   composition with stated rationale encouraged; >~30 min off-arc gets
109	   the detour flag.
110	
111	**Tool**: the ABA forward model (`hera/models/aba_trilayer/`) is the
112	primary arc-reader for fan features, per the investigation's Verify.
113	
114	Phase-2 arc: cheap discriminators before magnet hours; grid design
115	guards before any fan; model overlay + Verify before any feature
116	claim; iterate per the recipe's step 4. The call lands as the five-part
117	output contract, STYLE strength vocabulary, in the ana notebook.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## Session arc (expected shape — you drive, within each phase)
122	
123	1. Gates A→B per the agent prompt (SAFETIES = the operator-committed
124	   outer box; compare numbers to the card). Gate C: first-session
125	   branch — no references; liveness comes from the bring-up chain.
126	2. Phase 1, recipes 1–2 → exit report → **operator go**.
127	3. Phase 2, ladder → fans → Verify → the call.
128	
129	Wall-clock realism: phase 1 is minutes-to-tens-of-minutes per step;
130	phase 2's field work is hours-scale. Price everything; cheap-first
131	throughout. The phase gate is also the natural break if the session
132	splits across operator windows or days — phase 2 re-enters through
133	Gate A/B and the silent-precondition reads, not through re-doing
134	phase 1.
135	
136	## Timing + logistics
137	
138	- Magnet facts per the rig card; traverse is the dominant fan cost.
139	  Calibrate per-point and per-row from this session's first sweeps.
140	- Operator windows: confirm at start. Cryocooling is closed-loop on
141	  this rig — session length is operator time, not cryogen budget.
142	- The QSwitch is live but newly commissioned: any mux anomaly
143	  (state/`mc_fragment` mismatch, settle violations in Verify) is
144	  stop-and-report, not push-through.
145	
146	## [VERIFY] at session start
147	
148	- [ ] Operator has run the SAFETIES cell; values match the card's
149	      gate operating-limits table.
150	- [ ] Magnet at 0 T (set vs read).
151	- [ ] QSwitch routing maps + `settle_s` present in the card; bring-up
152	      log entry exists; **Si standing closures (lines 16/11) verified
153	      closed**.
154	- [ ] Heater ownership + max-T ceiling (if temperature work arises).
155	- [ ] Base T holding.
156	
157	## Session notes
158	
159	Same discipline as ever (`session_notes.md`, tagged entries). New
160	recipe surface this session (agent-driven, mux-automated contact
161	bring-up) — RECIPE FIX entries are a primary deliverable. The phase
162	split is new — note any thoughts on it.

1	# Device card — QC0426 (trilayer graphene) — round 2
2	
3	*Session device card for QC0426 on the **VTI** cryostat — round-2 HERA
4	live session (replication from a cooled start). Deployed into the
5	measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
6	**physical truth only**: what is wired, what the hardware is, and the
7	outer safety box. Operating ranges, calibrations, and characterization
8	are **deliberately absent — establishing them is the session** (see the
9	session brief). This session's data ids start at 0 in `./data/`.*
10	
11	## Identity
12	- **Device id**: `QC0426`
13	- **Material**: **trilayer graphene** (`3LGr`), **stacking order under
14	  investigation** — ABA (Bernal) and ABC (rhombohedral) trilayer have
15	  qualitatively different Landau-fan / quantum-Hall signatures and
16	  displacement-field dependence, and classifying the stacking from the
17	  fan-vs-D structure is this device's campaign goal. Form reads from the
18	  data; do not assert a stacking this card does not state.
19	- **Operator**: qingrui
20	- **Fridge**: **VTI (variable-temperature insert)** — *not* the
21	  dilution-fridge toploader. Base temperature this cooldown is
22	  **≈ 1.2–1.3 K**, not millikelvin.
23	- **Status**: **cold, wired, transport-uncharacterized for your
24	  purposes.** Loaded 2026-06-01; the device arrives as a characterizable
25	  unknown. Gate operating limits are provided (below); no CNP location
26	  and no contact rankings are on record — the device-init recipe chain
27	  (contact survey + CNP calibration) establishes those.
28	
29	## Gate stack (three gates, unusual drive wiring)
30	- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by the SRS DC205, not
31	  a Keithley** — in the data it appears as the column **`DC_bias`** (the
32	  DC205 voltage), and in sweep calls as `dc205_volt` (a
33	  `qcodes.Parameter` wrapping `k_tg.ramp_voltage`, `ramp_rate = 2`; the
34	  measure notebook's setup cells define it).
35	- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): hBN dielectric, driven by a **Keithley 2400**.
36	- **Si global back gate** (`k_si` / `k_2410`): doped-Si gate through
37	  **SiO₂**, driven by a second Keithley (`k_2410`). **The Si value is
38	  per-run — read `measurement_config`, never assume a campaign-wide
39	  constant.** Operating limit provided (below); pick a value within it
40	  per run (`silicon-backgate-survey` is not run this session).
41	- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
42	  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
43	  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
44	  ```python
45	  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
46	  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(15.6, 3)])           # 15.6 nm hBN
47	  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(12, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 12 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
48	  ```
49	  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
50	  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.
51	
52	## Gate operating limits — gate B contract
53	
54	**These are the gate operating limits for the session, provided by the
55	operator (not range-found this cooldown).** Commit them as the gate
56	validators at session start; staying inside them is safe for the
57	device. The Si operating *point* (a value within its range) is per-run;
58	read `measurement_config`.
59	
60	The SAFETIES cell in the measure notebook must commit **exactly these
61	numbers**; compare values, don't eyeball:
62	
63	| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| `dc205_volt` / `k_tg` | **[−6.0, +7.0] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
66	| `k_bg.volt` | **[−4.5, +4.5] V** | provided |
67	| `k_2410.volt` (Si) | **[−50, +50] V** | provided; operating point per-run |
68	| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 8.0 T** | protocol-enforced (driver has no soft-limit hook) |
69	
70	## Measurement setup (rig instruments wired this cooldown)
71	- **Gates**: top via **DC205** (`DC_bias`), back via **k_bg** Keithley,
72	  Si via **k_2410** Keithley.
73	- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0…sr3` live).

# Device card — QC0426 (trilayer graphene) — round 2

*Session device card for QC0426 on the **VTI** cryostat — round-2 HERA
live session (replication from a cooled start). Deployed into the
measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
**physical truth only**: what is wired, what the hardware is, and the
outer safety box. Operating ranges, calibrations, and characterization
are **deliberately absent — establishing them is the session** (see the
session brief). This session's data ids start at 0 in `./data/`.*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `QC0426`
- **Material**: **trilayer graphene** (`3LGr`), **stacking order under
  investigation** — ABA (Bernal) and ABC (rhombohedral) trilayer have
  qualitatively different Landau-fan / quantum-Hall signatures and
  displacement-field dependence, and classifying the stacking from the
  fan-vs-D structure is this device's campaign goal. Form reads from the
  data; do not assert a stacking this card does not state.
- **Operator**: qingrui
- **Fridge**: **VTI (variable-temperature insert)** — *not* the
  dilution-fridge toploader. Base temperature this cooldown is
  **≈ 1.2–1.3 K**, not millikelvin.
- **Status**: **cold, wired, transport-uncharacterized for your
  purposes.** Loaded 2026-06-01; the device arrives as a characterizable
  unknown. Gate operating limits are provided (below); no CNP location
  and no contact rankings are on record — the device-init recipe chain
  (contact survey + CNP calibration) establishes those.

## Gate stack (three gates, unusual drive wiring)
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by the SRS DC205, not
  a Keithley** — in the data it appears as the column **`DC_bias`** (the
  DC205 voltage), and in sweep calls as `dc205_volt` (a
  `qcodes.Parameter` wrapping `k_tg.ramp_voltage`, `ramp_rate = 2`; the
  measure notebook's setup cells define it).
- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): hBN dielectric, driven by a **Keithley 2400**.
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si` / `k_2410`): doped-Si gate through
  **SiO₂**, driven by a second Keithley (`k_2410`). **The Si value is
  per-run — read `measurement_config`, never assume a campaign-wide
  constant.** Operating limit provided (below); pick a value within it
  per run (`silicon-backgate-survey` is not run this session).
- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
  ```python
  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(15.6, 3)])           # 15.6 nm hBN
  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(12, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 12 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
  ```
  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.

## Gate operating limits — gate B contract

**These are the gate operating limits for the session, provided by the
operator (not range-found this cooldown).** Commit them as the gate
validators at session start; staying inside them is safe for the
device. The Si operating *point* (a value within its range) is per-run;
read `measurement_config`.

The SAFETIES cell in the measure notebook must commit **exactly these
numbers**; compare values, don't eyeball:

| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dc205_volt` / `k_tg` | **[−6.0, +7.0] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
| `k_bg.volt` | **[−4.5, +4.5] V** | provided |
| `k_2410.volt` (Si) | **[−50, +50] V** | provided; operating point per-run |
| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 8.0 T** | protocol-enforced (driver has no soft-limit hook) |

## Measurement setup (rig instruments wired this cooldown)
- **Gates**: top via **DC205** (`DC_bias`), back via **k_bg** Keithley,
  Si via **k_2410** Keithley.
- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0…sr3` live).
  Current-bias drive: **0.5 V through a 100 MΩ bias resistor**, lock-in
  frequency **≈ 13 Hz**.
- **Current channel**: **`sr0`** = drain current, **`sr0_gain = −1E6`**
  (Ithaco preamp gain). **Current is `I = sr0_X / sr0_gain`** — the
  explicit gain division is mandatory. Per-channel sensitivities are
  recorded per run in `measurement_config`.
- **Voltage channels**: `sr1, sr2, sr3` carry four-terminal voltages;
  **contact pairs are per-run** and live in `measurement_config` (with
  the QSwitch live, in the `mc_fragment` the mux writes), never in a
  global block.
- **Contact switching — QSwitch (QDevil) mux**: `drivers.QSwitch` +
  `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`. **Bring-up complete and validated
  (2026-06-14)** — ContactMux is live on this rig:
  - Wiring topology (2026-06-12 rewiring, final per the operator's
    routing slide): device pads bond to two Fischer cables; the
    QSwitch takes **F1 only**, and F2-riding contact pads are shorted
    onto spare F1 conductors at the breakout. **F1 fischer index =
    QSwitch line number.** TG and BG do **not** pass through the
    QSwitch (hardwired to their sources — fixed, unswitchable). Si
    passes through the QSwitch and back to the breakout box.
  - **Contact map** (label = position, T = top arc L→R, B = left side
    then bottom L→R; all switchable):

    | Label | Pad | Line | | Label | Pad | Line |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | T1 | F2-05 | 1 | | B1 | F2-37 | 8 |
    | T2 | F1-33 | 3 | | B2 | F2-21 | 17 |
    | T3 | F1-09 | 4 | | B3 | F1-28 | 23 |
    | T4 | F1-01 | 6 | | B4 | F1-12 | 22 |
    | T5 | F1-42 | 7 | | B5 | F1-20 | 20 |
    | T6 | F1-02 | 12 | | B6 | F1-44 | 19 |
    | T7 | F1-43 | 13 | | B7 | F1-03 | 18 |
    | | | | | B8 | F1-35 | 15 |

  - **Gates**: TG (DC205) and BG (K2400) **hardwired — no relay can
    touch them**. **Si (K2410) rides QSwitch lines 16 and 11** with
    standing closed relays ("keep 16/11 closed inside the QSwitch" —
    routed through the switch and back to the breakout box). Lines
    16/11 are **excluded from ContactMux's managed set** (never in the
    `lines` map), and **`qsw.reset()` is forbidden once Si is
    energized** — it opens the standing closures and drops the Si
    gate. **Si closures on lines 16/11 confirmed closed at bring-up
    (2026-06-14).**
  - **Instrument taps (BNC 1–8)**: 1 = sr1.V1, 2 = sr1.V2, 3 = sr2.V1,
    4 = sr2.V2, 5 = sr3.V1, 6 = sr3.V2, **7 = sr1.amplitude (AC
    source)**, **8 = sr0.V1 × −1e6 (measured AC current)**. ContactMux
    form: `breakouts = {"source": 7, "drain": 8, "sr1+": 1, "sr1-": 2,
    "sr2+": 3, "sr2-": 4, "sr3+": 5, "sr3-": 6}`. Worked example (per
    the routing slide): source T3 / drain T5 / measure T3–T4 ⇒ tap 7 →
    line 4, taps 1/2 → lines 4 and 6, tap 8 → line 7.
  - COM port: **ASRL4** (confirmed at bring-up 2026-06-14 — reconnected
    on ASRL4, not the expected ASRL3; Microchip VID_04D8 USB-CDC, with
    the DC205 and the logger-held Terranova gauge as the resident FTDI
    serials).
  - `settle_s` (calibrated relay settle at campaign time constant):
    **4 s** (calibrated 2026-06-14).
  - Bring-up: address **ASRL4**, `settle_s` **4 s**, Si 16/11 confirmed,
    validated 2026-06-14.
  ContactMux is **live**; `contact-survey-2t`'s automated flavor is

- **Magnet**: **FastBi1K5** — custom Ethernet-driven magnet controller
  (192.168.0.10), **not an AMI430**. Out-of-plane field in **Tesla**

- **Temperature / thermometry**: LakeShore controller; VTI base

## Notes / caveats

1	# Rig card — VTI
2	
3	*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
4	insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
5	`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
6	`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
7	in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
8	read-only on the repo.*
9	
10	## Identity
11	- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert, out-of-plane magnet
12	- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
13	  operating-edge questions
14	- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
15	  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
16	- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K
17	- **Status**: in service
18	
19	## Magnet
20	
21	- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
22	  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
23	  `mag` qcodes Parameter.
24	- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
25	- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
26	  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
27	  floor.
28	- **Set semantics**: `magnet.mag(target)` **blocks** until the field
29	  is reached (busy-polls the ramping flag, then 3 s dwell). A cell
30	  that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
31	- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
32	  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
33	  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `mag()` again
34	  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
35	  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
36	- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
37	  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; `mag()` raises above it). The
38	  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
39	  `magnet.mag.vals`) is what measurements obey.
40	- **Read-truth**: `mag()`'s get returns the **measured** output
41	  current × `T_per_A` (`GET:I:?`, 2-stage moving-average readback,
42	  ~41 ms lag ≈ 0.1 mT at our slew). The set-point is not readable as
43	  field; never infer field from the last set call.
44	- **Persistent-switch heater**: `heater_on()` / `heater_off()`, each
45	  blocks 10 s, **no field-matching check** before toggling —
46	  operator-only, with care.
47	- **Never re-traverse**: the fixed slow ramp makes field the expensive
48	  axis. Plan sweeps to start where the magnet sits and end where the
49	  next measurement needs it; alternate fan directions across
50	  iterations rather than returning to a preferred start field.
51	
52	## Thermometry & heaters
53	
54	- **Controller**: Lakeshore 335 (`drivers.Lakeshore_335`).
55	  Input A = sample-mount Cernox (`sample_temperature`, `KRDG? A`);
56	  input B = vaporizer Cernox (`vaporizer_temperature`, `KRDG? B`).
57	- **Sensors**: 2× CX-1030-CU-HT-0.3M (serials X225149, X225150),
58	  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
59	  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
60	  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
61	  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
62	  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
63	  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
64	  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
65	  (Bingcheng).
66	- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
67	  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
68	  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
69	  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
70	- **Control topology**: only the LS335 **sample loop is closed-loop**
71	  (input A ↔ sample-mount heater). PID / heater-range settings are a
72	  TODO even in the lab's own VTI doc. The **vaporizer / needle valve
73	  is operator-only, hands at the rig** — reaching and holding elevated
74	  T is operator craft; an agent's role is read-only settle-and-verify.
75	- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
76	  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
77	  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.
78	
79	## Safe operating envelope (T/B)
80	
81	- **Normal working window: no T/B co-constraints.** Elevated
82	  temperatures and fields within the rig's ordinary operating ranges
83	  are operationally fine. (Provenance: Aaron, 2026-06-12, via Zack.)
84	- **Consideration zone**: simultaneously **above ~10 T and above
85	  ~15 K** (early cut — Bingcheng, 2026-06-12, via Zack). Plans
86	  entering it get pre-checked with Bingcheng or the operator;
87	  Bingcheng adjudicates the edges.
88	- **Cryogen economics**: **closed-loop He system — consumption is not
89	  a session budget constraint** (Bingcheng/Qingrui, 2026-06-12, via
90	  Zack). Elevated-T holds still ride the vaporizer; no hold-time cap
91	  is documented for this rig.
92	
93	## Silent preconditions
94	
95	Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
96	bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
97	each. (LS335 instance is named `heater` in current templates.)
98	
99	| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| Sample temperature | `heater.sample_temperature()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
102	| Magnet field | `magnet.mag()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
103	| Vaporizer state | `heater.vaporizer_temperature()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
104	| PS heater / output | `magnet._status()` | heater on, output enabled (`mag()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |
105	
106	## Sweep stack & data layout
107	
108	- **Kernel stack**: the `sweep` package (measureme submodule — the
109	  single source of truth for sweep semantics); VTI notebooks build the
110	  station via `drivers.async_station`, a thin `sweep.Station` subclass
111	  (convergence onto sweep's own `AsyncStation` is backlogged):
112	
113	  ```python
114	  s = async_station(meas_config)
115	  s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P)
116	  s.sweep(param, vec, delay=...)                  # 1D
117	  s.multisweep([p1, p2], [v1, v2], delay=...)     # co-swept 1D (e.g. a D-line)
118	  s.megasweep(slow, svec, fast, fvec, ...)        # 2D
119	  s.multimegasweep([slow], [svec], [p1, p2], [v1, v2],
120	                   slow_delay=..., fast_delay=...)
121	  s.add_comment('<recipe-slug>')
122	  ```
123	
124	- **Comments are station-lifetime, not per-run**: every `add_comment`
125	  since station construction appears in every subsequent run's
126	  metadata. Rebuild the station (or scrub) between runs with different
127	  intent — stale inherited comments are a known trap.
128	- The basedir must exist before `async_station(...)` is constructed
129	  (the station writes `log.log` into it).
130	- **Data on disk**: each sweep writes
131	  `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/` — `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless,
132	  columns named in metadata), `metadata.json`, `plot.png`. `plot.png`
133	  is the live monitor, **not** the measurement — for rastered /
134	  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the
135	  TSV before any visual read.
136	- **Metadata delta**: two schemas coexist on this rig — older runs use
137	  singular keys (`param`, `slow_param`), the current build writes
138	  plural (`params`, `slow_params`) and adds `version`/`instruments`.
139	  Load through `sweep.sweep_load.pload` or `hera.analysis`; don't
140	  hand-roll key access.
141	
142	## Timing rules of thumb
143	
144	Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
145	current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
146	calibrating run.
147	
148	- **Per-point**: ~1.2 s/pt (held across the 2026-06-10 session's
149	  runs).
150	- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
151	  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
152	- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
153	  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
154	  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
155	  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
156	- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
157	  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
158	  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
159	  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
160	- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
161	  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
162	  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs.
163	
164	## Standard equipment
165	
166	Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
167	hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict. Bus
168	addresses move between sessions and are not documented here.
169	
170	- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
171	  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
172	- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
173	  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
174	  `measurement_config`.
175	- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud) — use
176	  `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp, deterministic dV/dt); the
177	  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
178	  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
179	- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
180	  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
181	  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
182	  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
183	  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
184	  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), pinned to **COM3/ASRL3**; the
185	  two resident serials are the DC205 and the logger-held Terranova
186	  gauge — only-two-ASRLs means the switch is unplugged, not moved.
187	  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
188	  (calibrate per campaign via the buffer-trace procedure in

# Rig card — VTI

*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
read-only on the repo.*

## Identity
- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert, out-of-plane magnet
- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
  operating-edge questions
- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K
- **Status**: in service

## Magnet

- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
  `mag` qcodes Parameter.
- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
  floor.
- **Set semantics**: `magnet.mag(target)` **blocks** until the field
  is reached (busy-polls the ramping flag, then 3 s dwell). A cell
  that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `mag()` again
  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; `mag()` raises above it). The
  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
  `magnet.mag.vals`) is what measurements obey.
- **Read-truth**: `mag()`'s get returns the **measured** output
  current × `T_per_A` (`GET:I:?`, 2-stage moving-average readback,
  ~41 ms lag ≈ 0.1 mT at our slew). The set-point is not readable as
  field; never infer field from the last set call.
- **Persistent-switch heater**: `heater_on()` / `heater_off()`, each
  blocks 10 s, **no field-matching check** before toggling —
  operator-only, with care.
- **Never re-traverse**: the fixed slow ramp makes field the expensive
  axis. Plan sweeps to start where the magnet sits and end where the
  next measurement needs it; alternate fan directions across
  iterations rather than returning to a preferred start field.

## Thermometry & heaters

- **Controller**: Lakeshore 335 (`drivers.Lakeshore_335`).
  Input A = sample-mount Cernox (`sample_temperature`, `KRDG? A`);
  input B = vaporizer Cernox (`vaporizer_temperature`, `KRDG? B`).
- **Sensors**: 2× CX-1030-CU-HT-0.3M (serials X225149, X225150),
  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
  (Bingcheng).
- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
- **Control topology**: only the LS335 **sample loop is closed-loop**
  (input A ↔ sample-mount heater). PID / heater-range settings are a
  TODO even in the lab's own VTI doc. The **vaporizer / needle valve
  is operator-only, hands at the rig** — reaching and holding elevated
  T is operator craft; an agent's role is read-only settle-and-verify.
- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.

## Safe operating envelope (T/B)

- **Normal working window: no T/B co-constraints.** Elevated
  temperatures and fields within the rig's ordinary operating ranges
  are operationally fine. (Provenance: Aaron, 2026-06-12, via Zack.)
- **Consideration zone**: simultaneously **above ~10 T and above
  ~15 K** (early cut — Bingcheng, 2026-06-12, via Zack). Plans
  entering it get pre-checked with Bingcheng or the operator;
  Bingcheng adjudicates the edges.
- **Cryogen economics**: **closed-loop He system — consumption is not
  a session budget constraint** (Bingcheng/Qingrui, 2026-06-12, via
  Zack). Elevated-T holds still ride the vaporizer; no hold-time cap
  is documented for this rig.

## Silent preconditions

Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
each. (LS335 instance is named `heater` in current templates.)

| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sample temperature | `heater.sample_temperature()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
| Magnet field | `magnet.mag()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
| Vaporizer state | `heater.vaporizer_temperature()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
| PS heater / output | `magnet._status()` | heater on, output enabled (`mag()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |

## Sweep stack & data layout

- **Kernel stack**: the `sweep` package (measureme submodule — the
  single source of truth for sweep semantics); VTI notebooks build the
  station via `drivers.async_station`, a thin `sweep.Station` subclass
  (convergence onto sweep's own `AsyncStation` is backlogged):

  ```python
  s = async_station(meas_config)
  s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P)
  s.sweep(param, vec, delay=...)                  # 1D
  s.multisweep([p1, p2], [v1, v2], delay=...)     # co-swept 1D (e.g. a D-line)
  s.megasweep(slow, svec, fast, fvec, ...)        # 2D
  s.multimegasweep([slow], [svec], [p1, p2], [v1, v2],
                   slow_delay=..., fast_delay=...)
  s.add_comment('<recipe-slug>')
  ```

- **Comments are station-lifetime, not per-run**: every `add_comment`
  since station construction appears in every subsequent run's
  metadata. Rebuild the station (or scrub) between runs with different
  intent — stale inherited comments are a known trap.
- The basedir must exist before `async_station(...)` is constructed
  (the station writes `log.log` into it).
- **Data on disk**: each sweep writes
  `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/` — `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless,
  columns named in metadata), `metadata.json`, `plot.png`. `plot.png`
  is the live monitor, **not** the measurement — for rastered /
  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the
  TSV before any visual read.
- **Metadata delta**: two schemas coexist on this rig — older runs use
  singular keys (`param`, `slow_param`), the current build writes
  plural (`params`, `slow_params`) and adds `version`/`instruments`.
  Load through `sweep.sweep_load.pload` or `hera.analysis`; don't
  hand-roll key access.

## Timing rules of thumb

Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
calibrating run.

- **Per-point**: ~1.2 s/pt (held across the 2026-06-10 session's
  runs).
- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs.

## Standard equipment

Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict. Bus
addresses move between sessions and are not documented here.

- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud) — use
  `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp, deterministic dV/dt); the
  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), pinned to **COM3/ASRL3**; the
  two resident serials are the DC205 and the logger-held Terranova
  gauge — only-two-ASRLs means the switch is unplugged, not moved.
  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
  (calibrate per campaign via the buffer-trace procedure in
  `hera/docs/vti/qswitch-smoke-test.md`). **Bring-up status: not yet
  blessed** — until the smoke-test's step-7 log has an entry,
  `ContactMux` is not live on this rig. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps
  are wiring → (per-device).
- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.

## Known quirks

- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
  to address unicode issues.
- **The LS335 has two masters**: a Grafana logger polls it alongside
  the measurement kernel, and VISA contention between them has killed
  a run. Coordinate with the operator before adding anything that
  polls the Lakeshore; single-poller fix is in the eng-backlog.
- The FastBi1K5 ramp busy-poll has no sleep — the driver hammers the
  socket for the entire ramp. Don't add concurrent socket traffic to
  the supply during a ramp (eng-backlog has the throttle fix).

## What this card does not carry

- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
  device card + SAFETIES cell.
- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

1	# Two-terminal contact survey
2	
3	*Base recipe, rig-agnostic. Switching mechanics are an instrument-class
4	conditional (switch matrix vs manual re-wiring) inside one procedure —
5	the loop's shape is the same; only who moves the cables differs. On a
6	rig with a switch matrix, `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux` is the house
7	interface, and the hard precondition for the automated flavor is a
8	**completed entry in that rig's mux bring-up record** — each mux rig
9	carries a smoke-test doc with a bring-up log (VTI:
10	`hera/docs/vti/qswitch-smoke-test.md`); no entry, no automated flavor.*
11	
12	## What
13	Per-contact-pair two-terminal characterization under identical
14	conditions: for each candidate pair, a short density sweep along the
15	calibrated CNP/D-line reading the drive current's gate response. Output:
16	a ranked contact table (pair → resistance scale, alive / high-R / dead,
17	response shape), bad contacts *localized* by shared-contact comparison,
18	and the chosen four-terminal configuration(s) for the campaign — all
19	written to the device card with run ids. Two flavors: the B = 0
20	baseline survey, and an at-field re-check (contacts re-rank in the
21	quantum-Hall regime).
22	
23	## When
24	- After `cnp-and-dline-calibration` and before committing to a 4T
25	  configuration: the survey sweeps along the calibrated D-line, which is
26	  what makes per-pair curves comparable, and the 4T choice is its
27	  product.
28	- **At-field flavor before any long at-field measurement**: a contact
29	  that couples fine at B = 0 can decouple in the QH regime (edge-state
30	  geometry, contact doping) — re-rank at the campaign field before
31	  pricing a fan on it.
32	- Mid-campaign, when a voltage channel goes flat or noisy: re-run the
33	  pairs sharing its contacts to localize.
34	
35	**Precondition — per-run contact truth.** Every run's
36	`measurement_config` records the pair actually measured (the survey is
37	useless if its metadata can't be read back later). With a switch matrix
38	that's `mux.mc_fragment()` merged per run; manually it's the
39	rewrite-config-in-the-same-cell discipline (`gate-range-finding`'s
40	truth precondition).
41	
42	## Why
43	A fan on a bad pair wastes hours; the survey costs minutes per pair. 2T
44	comes before 4T diagnostics because it needs no working voltage probes
45	and the pairwise structure localizes faults: a dead *pair* is ambiguous,
46	but a contact that kills every pair it appears in is identified —
47	provided the candidate set was chosen so each contact appears in at
48	least two pairs. The at-field flavor exists because the reference
49	campaign found it necessary (the QH regime re-ranks contacts) and
50	because at-field magnet time is expensive exactly when a dead channel is
51	discovered mid-fan.
52	
53	## Recipe
54	
55	**Step 0 — candidate set and price.** Enumerate from the device card's
56	contact map. All pairs is N(N−1)/2 — usually too many; pick a spanning
57	set where **every contact appears in ≥ 2 pairs** (attributability) and
58	the likely source/drain candidates appear in more. Price the loop:
59	N_pairs × (sweep time + switching overhead) — switching overhead is
60	seconds with a mux (`settle_s` from the smoke-test calibration), minutes
61	plus operator attention manually. State the number before starting.
62	
63	**Step 1 — freeze the conditions.** Gates follow the calibrated D-line
64	over the working n-window; screening gate at the campaign operating
65	point; excitation at or below the device-card ceiling; lock-in
66	sensitivity fixed (not autoranged — comparability across pairs is the
67	product). Same conditions for every pair, including the at-field
68	re-check (same line, same window, field added).
69	
70	**Step 2 — the loop.** Per pair: configure, record truth, sweep.
71	- **Switch-matrix flavor**: one cell can loop the whole set —
72	  `mux.select({...pair routing...})`, rebuild the station with
73	  `meas_config | mux.mc_fragment()`, `s.add_comment('contact-survey-2t')`
74	  plus a structured comment naming the pair, then the short n-sweep.
75	  **One run per pair**: never sweep contact-configuration as a fast

# Two-terminal contact survey

*Base recipe, rig-agnostic. Switching mechanics are an instrument-class
conditional (switch matrix vs manual re-wiring) inside one procedure —
the loop's shape is the same; only who moves the cables differs. On a
rig with a switch matrix, `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux` is the house
interface, and the hard precondition for the automated flavor is a
**completed entry in that rig's mux bring-up record** — each mux rig
carries a smoke-test doc with a bring-up log (VTI:
`hera/docs/vti/qswitch-smoke-test.md`); no entry, no automated flavor.*

## What
Per-contact-pair two-terminal characterization under identical
conditions: for each candidate pair, a short density sweep along the
calibrated CNP/D-line reading the drive current's gate response. Output:
a ranked contact table (pair → resistance scale, alive / high-R / dead,
response shape), bad contacts *localized* by shared-contact comparison,
and the chosen four-terminal configuration(s) for the campaign — all
written to the device card with run ids. Two flavors: the B = 0
baseline survey, and an at-field re-check (contacts re-rank in the
quantum-Hall regime).

## When
- After `cnp-and-dline-calibration` and before committing to a 4T
  configuration: the survey sweeps along the calibrated D-line, which is
  what makes per-pair curves comparable, and the 4T choice is its
  product.
- **At-field flavor before any long at-field measurement**: a contact
  that couples fine at B = 0 can decouple in the QH regime (edge-state
  geometry, contact doping) — re-rank at the campaign field before
  pricing a fan on it.
- Mid-campaign, when a voltage channel goes flat or noisy: re-run the
  pairs sharing its contacts to localize.

**Precondition — per-run contact truth.** Every run's
`measurement_config` records the pair actually measured (the survey is
useless if its metadata can't be read back later). With a switch matrix
that's `mux.mc_fragment()` merged per run; manually it's the
rewrite-config-in-the-same-cell discipline (`gate-range-finding`'s
truth precondition).

## Why
A fan on a bad pair wastes hours; the survey costs minutes per pair. 2T
comes before 4T diagnostics because it needs no working voltage probes
and the pairwise structure localizes faults: a dead *pair* is ambiguous,
but a contact that kills every pair it appears in is identified —
provided the candidate set was chosen so each contact appears in at
least two pairs. The at-field flavor exists because the reference
campaign found it necessary (the QH regime re-ranks contacts) and
because at-field magnet time is expensive exactly when a dead channel is
discovered mid-fan.

## Recipe

**Step 0 — candidate set and price.** Enumerate from the device card's
contact map. All pairs is N(N−1)/2 — usually too many; pick a spanning
set where **every contact appears in ≥ 2 pairs** (attributability) and
the likely source/drain candidates appear in more. Price the loop:
N_pairs × (sweep time + switching overhead) — switching overhead is
seconds with a mux (`settle_s` from the smoke-test calibration), minutes
plus operator attention manually. State the number before starting.

**Step 1 — freeze the conditions.** Gates follow the calibrated D-line
over the working n-window; screening gate at the campaign operating
point; excitation at or below the device-card ceiling; lock-in
sensitivity fixed (not autoranged — comparability across pairs is the
product). Same conditions for every pair, including the at-field
re-check (same line, same window, field added).

**Step 2 — the loop.** Per pair: configure, record truth, sweep.
- **Switch-matrix flavor**: one cell can loop the whole set —
  `mux.select({...pair routing...})`, rebuild the station with
  `meas_config | mux.mc_fragment()`, `s.add_comment('contact-survey-2t')`
  plus a structured comment naming the pair, then the short n-sweep.
  **One run per pair**: never sweep contact-configuration as a fast
  axis for survey data — per-run `measurement_config` is the truth
  surface and cannot carry per-point wiring (the config-as-sweep-axis
  trick is legitimate only for switch-transient tests, where the
  "data" is the transient itself).
- **Manual flavor**: one cell per pair (copy-and-edit, the search
  history stays in the notebook); the operator re-wires at the rack and
  the same cell rewrites `measurement_config` before sweeping.
  **Re-wire hygiene: zero the excitation before any cable move** (and
  ground/park lines per house practice) — plugging or unplugging drive
  lines on a gated, cold device with the excitation live risks
  transients through the contacts; restore the excitation in the same
  cell that rewrites the config, so the notebook record shows both.
- Either flavor: read the drive-current channel and whatever probe
  channels are wired; park gates between pairs only if the rig requires
  it (re-ramping costs time × N_pairs).

**Step 3 — rank and localize.** Per pair, form the resistance scale at
a reference density — choose it in the well-conducting regime away from
the CNP, use the *same* value for every pair, and state it in the
write-back — (drive amplitude over measured current, through the
rig's bias network per the device card) and classify: working / high-R
/ dead (no current at any n). Then the localization pass: a contact
present in ≥ 2 dead or high-R pairs while its partners work elsewhere
is the fault; a single dead pair with both contacts otherwise fine is a
pair-specific issue (wiring, not bond). Before declaring any contact
dead, check the false-positive modes: device grounded or tied at a
shared node (the `gate-current-sanity-check` failure catalog applies),
and — with a mux — that the recorded `qswitch_state` matches the
intended routing.

**Step 4 — at-field re-check (flavor).** At the campaign field, re-run
the loop on the surviving set only (cheaper). Plan the field move per
the rig's magnet discipline — get there once, schedule the survey when
the magnet is already at field if the campaign allows, never re-traverse
for it. Contacts re-rank; the 4T choice comes from pairs that survive
**at field**, not the B = 0 ranking. On screening-gate devices this is
one activity with `silicon-backgate-survey`'s at-field re-validation
(the reference campaign ran Si steps and per-pair checks as a single
6 T block) — schedule both on the same magnet excursion.

**Step 5 — choose and record.** Current path through the best
source/drain pair; voltage pairs on working contacts spanning the
device region(s) the science needs (region coverage matters on
possibly-inhomogeneous devices — channel disagreement downstream is
signal, and you want probes where it can show). Write to the device
card: ranking table, localization conclusions, chosen configuration(s),
run ids, and — with a mux — the routing dicts so the next session can
re-select them verbatim.

## Verify
- **Truth on disk**: after the first run of the loop, read its
  `metadata.json` back and confirm the pair entries (and
  `qswitch_state`, if muxed) are present and correct — *then* let the
  loop continue. Catching a truth gap after 12 runs re-does 12 runs.
- **Comparability**: diff the gate setpoints and excitation across the
  loop's metadata — identical by construction, so any drift is a bug in
  the loop cell.
- **Settle adequacy**: compare each run's first sweep point against its
  neighbors; a systematically off first point means switching transients
  are leaking into the data — raise `settle_s` (mux; re-calibrate per
  the smoke-test buffer-trace method) or add a post-rewire pause
  (manual).
- **Open-pair claims cite resolvability**: "no current" counts only
  with the sensitivity floor stated — at the recorded sensitivity and
  excitation, what resistance would have been measurable?

## Examples
- `vti/qingrui/20260601-QC0426-3LGr/measurement.ipynb` cells 116–154
  *(our-measurement)* — the manual flavor this recipe encodes. Cells
  127–140: per-pair 2T multisweeps along the sanitized CNP line at 6 T,
  Si ≈ +90 V — one `meas_config` rewrite per pair (05-33, 05-09, …),
  the drain contact moved by hand per run, pair truth carried in
  duplicate-key config entries and comment strings (the idiom
  `mc_fragment()` replaces). Cells 123–125: Si-gate steps as
  `multimegasweep` slow axis around the same block. Cells 141–154: 4T
  configurations re-checked at 6 T (09-01 / 01-42 / 42-02 wirings,
  excitation experiments at cells 149–151) — the step-4 + step-5 shape.
- `bsuo/CF01B1/measurement.ipynb` cells 21–52 *(our-measurement)* — the
  switch-matrix mechanics live, pre-`ContactMux`: `arrange` naming
  contacts/breakouts, `breakout`/`ground`/`unground` switching, the
  config-as-sweep-axis trick used for what it's for (switch-transient
  tests, cells 38–46, with the SR830 buffer-trace settle measurement
  this recipe's Verify and the smoke-test doc both lean on).

## Next
- **Configuration chosen**: the campaign's mapping recipes (`gatemap` /
  `nD-map` / `landau-fan`) on the blessed wiring; the device-card table
  is their contact-map input.
- **One contact kills multiple pairs**: operator escalation with the
  localization table — the decision (live with it, re-bond, warm up) is
  a physical-intervention call, not a recipe branch.
- **At-field re-rank changed the choice**: update the device card
  before the fan, and treat any B = 0-only prior ranking as superseded.
- **Channel goes bad mid-campaign**: re-enter at step 2 with the
  affected contacts' pairs only.

1	# CNP-line and D-line calibration
2	
3	*Base recipe, rig-agnostic. Mostly analysis: it consumes the cooldown's
4	first 0 T gate map and produces the validated (n, D) conversion and the
5	constant-D line designer that every coordinate-claiming recipe downstream
6	(`landau-fan`, `nD-map`, feature positions) inherits. The house
7	conversion is the capacitance form — `sharpelab_nb.gates`:
8	`stack_capacitance` / `calc_nD` / `calc_gate_voltages` — with the
9	device's numbers in the device card. (The legacy thickness-parametrized
10	`calculate_n_D` is the single-dielectric special case of the same
11	helpers; older notebooks also carry inline equivalents — use those only
12	to replot their own runs.)*
13	
14	## What
15	From a 0 T gate map: locate the charge-neutrality ridge per channel, fit
16	the CNP line in (V_tg, V_bg), refine the gate-capacitance **ratio** from
17	its slope (a fitted CNP slope dV_tg/dV_bg *is* −c_bg/c_tg), set the
18	density offset from its intercept, and emit constant-D gate-voltage
19	lines clipped to the validators. Output is a calibration contract
20	written to the device card: per-channel fits, the chosen (c_tg, c_bg)
21	with provenance split — **ratio: data-calibrated; absolute scale:
22	geometry prior until a quantum-Hall lever-arm check upgrades it** — the
23	offsets, a residual quality number, and the D-line designer parameters.
24	
25	## When
26	After `gate-range-finding` (validators committed) and a first `gatemap`
27	that shows the CNP crossing the swept window. Re-run when:
28	- the operating point of a screening gate changes (the CNP intercept
29	  shifts with it; the slope usually survives — verify, don't assume);
30	- `reentry-baseline` shows feature-position drift across a handover;
31	- quantum-Hall data lands and enables the lever-arm upgrade (step 5).
32	
33	No new sweeps are required if the gatemap is adequate; if the CNP exits
34	the window or is clipped (step 1 guard), this recipe specifies the map
35	extension and hands back to `gatemap`.
36	
37	## Why
38	Every (n, D)-coordinate claim downstream inherits this calibration:
39	wrong capacitances tilt a fan's co-swept fast axis (the "fixed D" line
40	silently varies in D), shift every filling-factor assignment, and move
41	feature positions between sessions. The CNP slope is the cheapest
42	precise calibration in the corpus — one polyfit on a map you already
43	have — and it measures exactly the quantity the conversion needs
44	(c_bg/c_tg). What it does **not** measure is the absolute scale: slope
45	and intercept are invariant under c → λc, so n and D magnitudes carry
46	the geometry prior's uncertainty until ray slopes (dn/dB = ν·e/h) or
47	SdH frequencies pin the scale. Keep the two tiers separate in every
48	write-back; an absolute-n claim quoted at ratio-grade precision is a
49	provenance error (STYLE rule 5).
50	
51	## Recipe
52	
53	**Step 0 — inputs.** Re-form the gate map from the TSV per channel
54	(`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement), with the device
55	card's channel arithmetic — including any mandatory gain division on the
56	current channel. Pull the dielectric-stack prior from the card and form
57	prior capacitances: `c = stack_capacitance([(t_nm, kappa), ...])` per
58	gate (series stacks — e.g. hBN over SiO₂ — are first-class).
59	
60	**Step 1 — extract the CNP ridge, per channel.** For each four-terminal
61	channel separately (never average channels — on a mosaic device the
62	channels disagree and the disagreement is signal, not noise): along each
63	gate-map row, locate the Rxx maximum across the fast axis. Smooth before
64	argmax when noisy (a 1D gaussian along the fast axis is the corpus
65	idiom). Two guards:
66	- **edge-clipped rows**: a row whose maximum sits at the swept-window
67	  edge has not located the CNP — exclude it from the fit and report the
68	  surviving row coverage; many clipped rows means the map is inadequate
69	  (see When).
70	- **competing maxima**: away from the CNP, contact-driven features or
71	  secondary peaks can outrun the CNP maximum. Restrict the argmax to a
72	  window around the visually-continuous ridge, or enforce continuity
73	  row-to-row; a ridge that jumps discontinuously is two features, not
74	  one line.
75	
76	**Step 2 — fit, per channel.** Linear fit (`np.polyfit`) of ridge
77	position vs row coordinate; report slope and intercept per channel with
78	fit residuals. **State the axis orientation with the fit**: the
79	`c_bg/c_tg = −slope` reading in step 3 assumes the ridge position is
80	V_tg (fast axis) fitted against V_bg rows — a transposed map yields the
81	*inverted* ratio (e.g. 1.3 ↔ 0.77) with no other symptom until the
82	Verify geometry check; name which gate was which axis in the write-back. Read the residuals before trusting the line: structured
83	curvature (quantum capacitance, screening nonlinearity) makes a linear
84	slope window-dependent — if present, fit over the operating window the
85	campaign will actually use and say so. Cross-channel check: slopes
86	agreeing to a few percent → one calibration for the device *(heuristic
87	threshold — n = 1 device to date; better: compare the disagreement
88	against the per-channel fit residuals and say which bound you used)*;
89	disagreement beyond that is real spatial variation — keep per-channel
90	calibrations, flag it, and carry the channel question forward (it feeds
91	channel triage in the stacking/feature recipes; this recipe records the
92	disagreement, it does not interpret it).
93	
94	**Step 3 — update the conversion.** From the chosen fit:
95	- **ratio**: `c_bg/c_tg = −slope`. Hold the better-constrained gate's
96	  capacitance at its stack prior and set the other from the ratio
97	  (heuristic — usually the simple single-dielectric gate is the anchor;
98	  state which you anchored).
99	- **density offset**: choose `n_offset` so the fitted line maps to
100	  n = 0: with `b` the V_tg intercept at V_bg = 0,
101	  `n_offset = -calc_nD(b, 0, c_tg, c_bg)[0]`.
102	- **D offset**: leave 0 unless the device exhibits a feature that
103	  physically locates D = 0 (e.g. a symmetric response in ±D); if you
104	  set it, cite the feature. An unexamined D_offset = 0 is itself a
105	  stated assumption — say it.
106	- **closure check**: `calc_nD` along the fitted ridge must return
107	  n ≈ 0; quote the max |n| residual as the calibration quality number.
108	
109	**Step 4 — design constant-D lines.** Generate gate vectors with
110	`calc_gate_voltages(ns, D0*ones, c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=...)` and **clip
111	to the committed validators by dropping out-of-range points, not
112	clamping them** (clamping bends the line in (n, D); dropping shortens
113	it). Report the *realized* n-window per D after clipping — at large |D|
114	it can be much narrower than requested, and a fan designed to the
115	requested window would silently lose rows. Design-time guards per STYLE
116	rule 12: point density along n sized to the finest expected feature,
117	stated in the proposing cell. Any run executed under this recipe (a
118	confirmation cut along a designed line) tags
119	`s.add_comment('cnp-and-dline-calibration')`.
120	
121	**Step 5 — write back.** Device card gets: per-channel slope/intercept
122	(+ run id of the source map), chosen (c_tg, c_bg) with the two-tier
123	provenance, offsets, residual quality, realized D-line table, and the
124	explicit upgrade path: *absolute scale pending quantum-Hall lever-arm
125	check* — when field data exists, ray slopes must quantize
126	(dn/dB = ν·e/h); a non-integer Δν spacing means the scale is wrong and
127	every ν claim inherits the error (recalibrate before classifying).
128	
129	## Verify
130	- **Roundtrip**: designed D-line vectors → `calc_nD` → D constant to
131	  numerical precision and n monotonic across the realized window.
132	- **Overlay**: fitted line drawn over the re-formed per-channel map —
133	  the ridge and the fit must track by eye; a fit that misses the ridge
134	  passed the math and failed the extraction (step 1 guards).
135	- **Geometry sanity**: compare the fitted ratio against the stack
136	  prior's ratio; agreement is confirmation, disagreement at the tens-of-
137	  percent level means a wrong thickness/κ in the card or a wrong gate
138	  assignment in the map axes — resolve before writing back.
139	- **Lever-arm upgrade** (when field data exists): the step-5 check.
140	
141	## Examples
142	- `vti/qingrui/20260601-QC0426-3LGr` *(our-measurement)* — the worked
143	  chain this recipe encodes. Measure cells 81–88: the 0 T TG–BG
144	  megasweep pair (197-pt back-gate rows). Analysis cells 10–11: the
145	  per-row argmax + `polyfit` extraction, cell 11 adding
146	  `gaussian_filter1d` smoothing — yielding `Vtg = −1.3·Vbg + 0.06`
147	  per the Rxx channels. Analysis cell 15: `sanitize_tg_bg`, the
148	  clip-by-dropping D-line designer this recipe's step 4 generalizes.
149	  Analysis cell 24: the inline capacitance `calc_nD` (t_tg = 15.6 nm,
150	  t_bg = 12 nm, κ_hBN = 3) — now canonical in `sharpelab_nb.gates`; on
151	  this device the geometry ratio (15.6/12 = 1.3) and the fitted slope
152	  agreed exactly, the happy case of the Verify geometry-sanity check.
153	  The campaign's D-line offset table (line constant ≈ −8·D) is device
154	  card content, consumed by the fan-design cells (analysis 50/58/61).
155	- Toploader corpus *(citation)*: `gatemap.md` defers CNP extraction to
156	  a then-unwritten recipe, and `landau-fan.md` names an SdH-frequency
157	  `cap-ratio-calibration` (still deferred) as the independent
158	  cross-method. This recipe is the CNP-slope method; the SdH method,
159	  when written, refines the same (c_tg, c_bg) from fan data and slots
160	  into step 5's upgrade path.
161	
162	## Next
163	- Default: the campaign's first designed measurement — the D-lines feed
164	  `landau-fan` fast axes and `nD-map` polygons; the realized-window
165	  table from step 4 is the input to their wall-clock pricing.
166	- Quantum-Hall data lands: run the lever-arm check (step 5); on failure,
167	  recalibrate and re-emit the D-line table before any ν assignment.
168	- Per-channel slopes disagree: carry the per-channel calibrations into
169	  the campaign's channel-triage step (`trilayer-stacking-id` step 2 or
170	  equivalent); do not average them away.
171	- CNP clipped or absent in the map: extend the `gatemap` window (or
172	  revisit `silicon-backgate-survey` — a screening-gate operating point
173	  can move the CNP into reach), then re-enter at step 1.
